D.treatment: journal articles with peer review and rigorous editing

cells.quote: Journal articles reflect more mature research efforts, more intense peer review and more rigorous editing than conference papers.
cells.note: Editorial comparison, not an empirical treatment study.

cells.quote: Virtually all published papers went through extensive critique and revision. Although it may not be visible to most readers, all papers had clearer organization and stronger arguments as a result of the review process — even though they may have been based on conference papers or dissertations that had already benefited from a great deal of review and editing.
cells.note: Editorial observation without a measured comparison or reported effect size.

cells.quote: In the years 1997 –2001 we had a number of special issues on topics such as authoring systems, collaborative learning, modelling teaching, educational dialogues and web-based teaching, all of which I feel played a significant part in developing those sub-fields of AIED.
cells.note: The author presents this as a personal retrospective judgement; no comparison condition or measured outcome is reported.

D.treatment: Articles with at least 100 Google Scholar citations
D.comparison: Articles with fewer than 100 Google Scholar citations

O.outcome_detail: Eligibility for inclusion among the anniversary issue's invited articles

cells.quote: Rigorous scholarly standards demanded an objective definition of what it means to be highly-cited! We settled on 100 citations as listed in Google Scholar as our inclusion criterion.
cells.note: This is an editorial selection rule, not an empirical learning comparison or outcome test.
